answer: Require agents to stake a slowly maturing reputation bond before they can vote or claim rewards: like a glacier, trust accumulates only over many epochs of consistent honest work, so a fresh fake identity starts with nothing. Each agent's record is public and tamper-evident — a marble ledger where every action is etched and visible — and attestations are cross-checked against crystal-clear on-chain history. An attacker would need to fund and age hundreds of identities for months, making a Sybil flood cost far more than any reward it could extract.
